hypotheses.title: Uniform Certified SAT-Circuit Error Constructor Conjecture
hypotheses.statement: For every constant k there is a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm E that, given n in unary and a Boolean circuit C of size at most n^k on the canonical encodings of length-n CNF formulas, outputs a polynomial-size certificate of one of the following: (i) a CNF G and satisfying assignment a with C(G)=0; (ii) a canonically padded terminal restriction G that is syntactically false with C(G)=1; or (iii) a CNF G and its two canonical first-unset-variable restrictions G_0,G_1 with C(G) different from C(G_0) OR C(G_1).
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: Every n^k-size circuit purporting to decide SAT would have a polynomial-time constructible, independently checkable error, so SAT would not be in SIZE(n^k) for every k. Hence SAT would not be in P/poly and P would differ from NP.
hypotheses.proof_role: DIRECT_BRIDGE: replace the fixed anti-checker list of H031 by a circuit-indexed local error certificate whose negative cases do not require a general coNP certificate.
hypotheses.next_gate: Construct E from the range-avoidance route H056, with a fixed-length padding convention and a proof that every avoided output yields one of the three certificate types.
hypotheses.delta_from_parents: H060 removes H031's unresolved polynomial UNSAT-certificate requirement by allowing a locally checkable Shannon self-reduction inconsistency, while making the constructor explicitly take the candidate circuit as input.
falsification_conditions: A polynomial-size SAT circuit for which E outputs no valid certificate at infinitely many lengths.
A certificate type whose verification does not logically imply that C disagrees with SAT under the fixed encoding.
hypotheses.claim_boundary: The local certificate lemma does not construct the initial error formula. H060 remains a circuit-lower-bound conjecture, not a proved SAT anti-checker.

hypotheses.title: DNNF-Safe Interface Typing Obstruction Conjecture
hypotheses.statement: There is a polynomial-time checkable support typing for finite-gate elimination interfaces such that every H041 run whose AND-like compositions have disjoint original-variable supports and whose OR-like compositions are certified deterministic compiles with polynomial overhead into an ordinary DNNF for the original CNF. Consequently, on the explicit DNNF-hard families used against H016, every polynomial-size H041 run must contain a certified composition violating this DNNF-safe typing discipline.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: The conjecture would convert H050 into a precise structural theorem: any surviving H041 algorithm must exploit nondecomposable overlap or nondeterministic union rather than hiding behind an undefined interface language.
hypotheses.proof_role: ADVERSARIAL_BRIDGE: isolate the exact semantic escape that a proof-carrying elimination mechanism needs in order to avoid known DNNF lower bounds.
hypotheses.next_gate: Formalize the interface gate semantics and prove the compilation induction, or exhibit one valid H041 template that satisfies the typing rules but cannot be represented by polynomial-size DNNF.
hypotheses.delta_from_parents: H061 narrows the all-or-nothing simulation claim H050 to an explicit DNNF-safe subclass and turns the destroyed H016 projection argument into a mandatory structural escape condition for H041.
falsification_conditions: A valid polynomial-size H041 run on a DNNF-hard family that obeys the stated typing discipline but has no polynomial DNNF translation.
A finite interface gate whose certified semantics invalidates the support-set induction while still meeting all H041 requirements.
hypotheses.claim_boundary: H061 does not claim that every H041 run is DNNF-safe; it identifies a subclass and a necessary escape condition.

hypotheses.title: Explicit Affine-Substitution-Stable Mixed Expander Conjecture
hypotheses.statement: There exist constants delta>0 and k and an explicit polynomial-time constructible CNF family M_n consisting of a bounded-degree XOR expander core coupled to a non-affine gadget such that, after any polynomial sequence of certified affine substitutions, Gaussian eliminations, and fan-in-two definitional rewrites allowed by H017 or H042, every polynomial-size residual representation has primal treewidth at least n^delta.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: M_n would instantiate H053 and H028, destroying the universal parity-core and affine-cardinality decomposition routes H017 and H042 unless they incur superpolynomial size.
hypotheses.proof_role: ADVERSARIAL_TARGET: replace the random-like target of H053 by one explicit family whose non-affine expansion is stable under the exact affine operations of the constructive compilers.
hypotheses.next_gate: Build the non-affine gadget from an explicit lossless expander or pseudorandom restriction construction and prove a minor or separator lower bound after arbitrary certified affine substitution.
hypotheses.delta_from_parents: H062 strengthens H053 from an existence-style mixed family to a quantified explicit stability theorem against the exact substitutions admitted by both surviving decomposition mechanisms.
falsification_conditions: A permitted polynomial-size decomposition of M_n with O(log n) residual treewidth.
An affine substitution sequence that collapses the proposed non-affine expansion while respecting all certificates.
hypotheses.claim_boundary: No explicit M_n or stability proof is supplied in this cycle; the conjecture is a target-selection refinement.

hypotheses.title: Canonical Polynomial-Conflict CDCL-over-Parities Conjecture
hypotheses.statement: There exist fixed deterministic polynomial-time policies for branching on literals or affine equations, restart scheduling, linear-clause learning, and deletion such that CDCL over parities, with polynomial memory and polynomial-time checkable Res(XOR) proof logging, solves every CNF in polynomially many conflicts and recovers a satisfying assignment on satisfiable inputs.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: The solver would decide CNF-SAT in deterministic polynomial time and imply P = NP.
hypotheses.proof_role: DIRECT_ALGORITHM: replace the resolution-limited H048 policy by a precisely stronger parity-learning solver whose proof traces live in Res(XOR).
hypotheses.next_gate: Fix one executable policy and attack it with the mixed family H062/H064 and with unrestricted Res(XOR) proof-size lower-bound candidates.
hypotheses.delta_from_parents: H063 accepts the decisive failure of ordinary CDCL in H048 and changes the proof system itself by permitting arbitrary parity decisions and learned linear clauses rather than merely extracting pre-existing XOR templates.
falsification_conditions: An explicit CNF family requiring superpolynomial conflicts for the exact policy.
A soundness, completeness, proof-logging, memory, or witness-recovery failure on a concrete input.
hypotheses.claim_boundary: Ordinary resolution lower bounds do not directly refute H063 because its logged proof system is stronger. No universal policy is known.

hypotheses.title: Mixed-Residual Unrestricted Res(XOR) Lower-Bound Conjecture
hypotheses.statement: The explicit family M_n demanded by H062 has n^omega(1) size lower bounds for unrestricted dag-like Resolution-over-Parities refutations, with the encoding length of every affine equation and linear clause charged to proof size.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: This would instantiate the broad H005 frontier with an explicit mixed family, refute the polynomial-conflict promise in H063 on unsatisfiable inputs, and advance the lower-bound route toward stronger bounded-depth Frege systems.
hypotheses.proof_role: TARGET_SELECTION: connect the affine-stable residual construction to the exact unrestricted proof system generated by the parity-enhanced solver.
hypotheses.next_gate: Define M_n explicitly, prove a semantic or communication measure invariant under unrestricted linear-clause resolution, and rule out short Gaussian-style refutations.
hypotheses.delta_from_parents: H064 selects the same mixed family used against structural compilers as the concrete hard target for unrestricted Res(XOR), linking a constructive solver descendant directly to its adversarial proof-complexity counterpart.
falsification_conditions: Polynomial-size unrestricted Res(XOR) refutations of M_n.
A theorem that the mixed gadget admits a polynomial Gaussian or linear-clause elimination proof.
hypotheses.claim_boundary: Known bounded-depth or restricted Res(XOR) lower bounds do not establish H064.
